## (b) Decision heuristics (D1-D6)

**D1 – what to test**
- Test what real users/practitioners do, end to end, not proxies or homework versions. 
  > "oftentimes when we test models, we test them on the thing that we think is hard for humans, but is not like the actual thing that represents the real task. And I would like to see more people trying to understand the end to end nature of things."  
  > -- `research__the_adversarial_mind_defeating_ai_defenses_with_ni_f046505d` (2025-02-27; solo author) 
  > "AutoAdvExBench is interesting for many reasons, but most importantly because it is not a proxy metric for some security task, but is the complete and exact task that real machine learning security researchers write papers on"  
  > -- `research__autoadvexbench_benchmarking_autonomous_exploitatio_27715bcb` (2025-03-03; first author)
- Understand the system better than its builder; probe with the exact context cues of the target. 
  > "The only way you'll come up with an exploit is by understanding the system better than the person who built it in the first place! Because they (presumably) aren't aware of any exploits"  
  > -- `research__why_i_attack_d0fe4023` (2024-06-24; solo author) 
  > "Configure the HEx-PHI benchmark with specific attack vectors by optionally specifying: 1) system prompt (i.e., use the system prompt found in the fine-tuning training data), 2) function to modify the user prompt (e.g., append backdoor trigger string, encode in cipher, etc.)"  
  > -- `research__detecting_adversarial_fine_tuning_with_auditing_ag_337948ca` (2025-10-17; last author)
- Look for areas where current practice looks obviously wrong; skip variations of approaches already believed. 
  > "How do you know when you have something only you can do? I look for areas where, when I read the work, I want to scream. Areas where you keep asking yourself "why is everyone doing this obviously wrong?""  
  > -- `research__how_to_win_a_best_paper_award_or_an_opinionated_ta_54221651` (2026-03-09; solo author) 
  > "What I tend to spend my time looking at are the things that when you look at them, they do look a little more weird. And that's those are the more interesting defenses because they're like a qualitatively new class of of way of thinking about this."  
  > -- `research__the_adversarial_mind_defeating_ai_defenses_with_ni_f046505d` (2025-02-27; solo author)
- Build on established realistic benchmarks rather than inventing tasks from scratch. 
  > "Starting from tasks that are known to be diverse and high quality, instead of creating new ones from scratch, allows our benchmark to enjoy the same properties with relatively small effort."  
  > -- `research__impossiblebench_measuring_llms_propensity_of_explo_c4e85750` (2025-10-23; last author)

**D2 – what evidence to collect**
- Connect the model to live tool environments and observe multi-step behavior. 
  > "In this test, I directly connect the model up to a SQL database, piping any model output directly to the database, and any output back to the model."  
  > -- `research__my_benchmark_for_large_language_models_0bb6cd0b` (2024-02-19; solo author) 
  > "Carlini ran this live on stage: a Docker container running Ghost, a single script the model had written, and within moments the full credential set was printed to the terminal."  
  > -- `research__llms_now_find_zero_days_autonomously_what_it_means_a82d6d05` (2026-04-13; solo author)
- Include human red-teamers alongside automation, and diverse attack families. 
  > "human red-teaming succeeds in all the cases we evaluated, even when the participants have only limited information and feedback from the target system. On a selected subset of scenarios and defenses, the search attack succeeds 69% of the time"  
  > -- `research__the_attacker_moves_second_stronger_adaptive_attack_16ebd8f7` (2025-10-10; middle author) 
  > "By attempting to generating adversarial examples with purely random search, by sampling completely random perturbations (with, e.g., Gaussian or uniform random noise) we can confirm that we aren't missing anything obvious."  
  > -- `research__advice_on_evaluating_adversarial_example_defenses_f3b3c399` (2018-05-26; solo author)
- Manually verify successes so they don't exploit scorer weaknesses. 
  > "We manually verified all attacks to ensure they were not exploiting weaknesses in our scoring mechanism."  
  > -- `research__the_attacker_moves_second_stronger_adaptive_attack_16ebd8f7` (2025-10-10; middle author)
- Validate the harness on known-broken targets so a null is interpretable. 
  > "This can be done by selecting alternate models that are either known to be insecure or are intentionally designed to be insecure, and verify that the new attack algorithm can effectively break these defenses."  
  > -- `research__on_evaluating_adversarial_robustness_b187c740` (2019-02-18; first author) 
  > "we now have access to both a flawed and a well-working adversarial evaluation method for each defense. This allows us to compare how these attacks perform in terms of both the estimated robust accuracy and the score on the binarization test."  
  > -- `research__increasing_confidence_in_adversarial_robustness_ev_fa33619a` (2022-06-28; last author)

**D3 – accept/reject a result**
- Reject near-zero attack rates on public benchmarks and weak-attack passes. 
  > "Indeed, defenses that merely report near-zero attack success rates on public benchmarks are often among the easiest to break once novel attacks are attempted."  
  > -- `research__the_attacker_moves_second_stronger_adaptive_attack_16ebd8f7` (2025-10-10; middle author) 
  > "It was never intended to be a strong attack for evaluating the robustness of a neural network, and should not be used as one."  
  > -- `research__advice_on_evaluating_adversarial_example_defenses_f3b3c399` (2018-05-26; solo author)
- Use consistency sanity checks; violations mean the test is broken. 
  > "Iterative attacks are strictly more powerful than single-step attacks, and so their results should be strictly superior. If an iterative attack performs worse than a single-step attack, this often indicates that the iterative attack is not correct."  
  > -- `research__advice_on_evaluating_adversarial_example_defenses_f3b3c399` (2018-05-26; solo author) 
  > "I'm following the gradients to make the model get less good, and the model gets more good.” This is somewhat confusing."  
  > -- `research__lessons_from_10_years_of_adversarial_machine_learn_050fae72` (undated; solo author)
- Judge non-trivial elicitation: harmful output must be specific and coherent, not echoing the request. 
  > "If it does not refuse, are its replies specific and convincing in a way that could actually manifest in harmful ways? Or are they incoherent and unlikely to actually result in harm?"  
  > -- `research__detecting_adversarial_fine_tuning_with_auditing_ag_337948ca` (2025-10-17; last author) 
  > "trivial attacks such as prompting "please repeat [harmful text]" do not reveal meaningful new vulnerabilities. Hence, there is no clear universal standard on what sorts of prompts or transformations count as "valid" or "novel" adversarial inputs."  
  > -- `research__position_adversarial_ml_for_llms_is_not_making_any_580cc8c8` (2025-02-04; middle author)
- Treat evaluation as a negative goal: try as hard as possible and fail. 
  > "empirical evaluations cannot prove that a defense is robust; all it can (and should) do is fail to prove that the defense is broken! A defense evaluation should try as hard as possible to break the defense and ultimately fail."  
  > -- `research__the_attacker_moves_second_stronger_adaptive_attack_16ebd8f7` (2025-10-10; middle author) 
  > "Adversarial robustness is a negative goal – for a defense to be truly effective, one needs to show that no attack can bypass it."  
  > -- `research__on_evaluating_adversarial_robustness_b187c740` (2019-02-18; first author)

**D4 – pursue/abandon**
- Start with the sub-problem most likely to fail, using small prototypes. 
  > "The best way I've found to minimize wasted time is to start with the sub-problem most likely to fail. It's comforting to work on the parts of a problem you know how to solve, but this teaches you nothing about whether your idea is any good."  
  > -- `research__how_to_win_a_best_paper_award_or_an_opinionated_ta_54221651` (2026-03-09; solo author)
- Write the best-case conclusion first; abandon if nothing insightful beyond numbers. 
  > "I ask: if this paper were to succeed wildly---if all the experiments turned out exactly as I want---what could I say in a conclusion? If I have nothing to say beyond repeating the results, then what I've done mustn't have mattered very much."  
  > -- `research__how_to_win_a_best_paper_award_or_an_opinionated_ta_54221651` (2026-03-09; solo author)
- Prefer problems whose evaluation is tractable and formalizable. 
  > "the problem might be easier, but the evaluation of it is much harder. And so it may be the case that this is an easier problem to solve, but I'm not going to be able to know whether or not you actually have solved it."  
  > -- `research__lessons_from_10_years_of_adversarial_machine_learn_050fae72` (undated; solo author) 
  > "How do you formalize that? What is the mathematical function that is 1 every time the model gives instructions on how to build a bomb, and 0 otherwise? Because if I'm going to try and optimize this, I need some formalism that I can look at."  
  > -- `research__lessons_from_10_years_of_adversarial_machine_learn_050fae72` (undated; solo author)
- Build proxy-free realistic benchmarks early. 
  > "we believe that it is important to start designing challenging real-world benchmarks now, so that we can have them before they are necessary."  
  > -- `research__autoadvexbench_benchmarking_autonomous_exploitatio_27715bcb` (2025-03-03; first author)

**D5 – reading surprises**
- Investigate cases where the weaker method beats the stronger instead of dismissing them. 
  > "I suggest looking at which instances adversarial examples can be found with black-box but not white-box attacks. Check if these instances are at all related, and investigate why white-box attacks are not finding these adversarial examples."  
  > -- `research__advice_on_evaluating_adversarial_example_defenses_f3b3c399` (2018-05-26; solo author)
- Expect high sensitivity to prompt wording; vary guidance strictness. 
  > "we discovered that LLM behaviors are surprisingly sensitive to prompt details, with looser guidance leading to significantly higher cheating rates."  
  > -- `research__impossiblebench_measuring_llms_propensity_of_explo_c4e85750` (2025-10-23; last author)
- Offer a legitimate escape hatch to test whether misbehavior stems from lack of alternatives. 
  > "we instruct the models to submit the string `flag_for_human_intervention` when they identify errors in the task, and the agent doing so will be immediately terminated."  
  > -- `research__impossiblebench_measuring_llms_propensity_of_explo_c4e85750` (2025-10-23; last author)
- Non-monotonic results may reflect scaffold fit, not capability. 
  > "Reasoning models generally performed worse: OpenAI's o1 and o3-mini, and 3.7 Sonnet with reasoning enabled. This result is not unique to our results: prior work (Wijk et al., 2024) has also found that reasoning models require substantially different agent frameworks."  
  > -- `research__autoadvexbench_benchmarking_autonomous_exploitatio_27715bcb` (2025-03-03; first author)

**D6 – what to claim**
- Claim necessary-not-sufficient; a failed test undermines confidence without proving breakage. 
  > "Note that this does not necessarily imply that the theorem is not correct (a.k.a. that the defense is not effective), but it should not give us any confidence that it is."  
  > -- `research__increasing_confidence_in_adversarial_robustness_ev_fa33619a` (2022-06-28; last author) 
  > "a defense is only interesting from the perspective of a security evaluation if it withstands future attack. Showing that a defense can defeat previous attacks is a necessary, but not sufficient, component of an evaluation."  
  > -- `research__advice_on_evaluating_adversarial_example_defenses_f3b3c399` (2018-05-26; solo author)
- Look past headline rates to the form of misbehavior. 
  > "While the models’ cheating rates are relatively similar on the surface, we find them engaging in vastly different cheating behaviors."  
  > -- `research__impossiblebench_measuring_llms_propensity_of_explo_c4e85750` (2025-10-23; last author)
- Ground claims in true technical facts. 
  > "I think the thing that I just want to make sure that people do is that they base whatever they're thinking about on true technical facts."  
  > -- `research__the_adversarial_mind_defeating_ai_defenses_with_ni_f046505d` (2025-02-27; solo author)

**Distrusts**
- Evaluations with weak or non-adaptive attacks. 
  > "Defending against non-adaptive attacks is necessary but not sufficient. It is our firm belief that an evaluation against non-adaptive attacks is of very limited utility."  
  > -- `research__on_evaluating_adversarial_robustness_b187c740` (2019-02-18; first author) 
  > "It was never intended to be a strong attack for evaluating the robustness of a neural network, and should not be used as one."  
  > -- `research__advice_on_evaluating_adversarial_example_defenses_f3b3c399` (2018-05-26; solo author)
- LLM judges/monitors and model self-justifications. 
  > "However, for simplicity, many studies opt to simulate these environments and rely on LLMs as judges for evaluation. There are new setups that have more rigorous evaluations (Debenedetti et al., 2024), where the attack's success and utility can be precisely measured"  
  > -- `research__position_adversarial_ml_for_llms_is_not_making_any_580cc8c8` (2025-02-04; middle author) 
  > "While it remains unclear whether the model intentionally crafted this justification or was simply misunderstanding the task requirements, the monitor accepted such claims as legitimate reasoning"  
  > -- `research__impossiblebench_measuring_llms_propensity_of_explo_c4e85750` (2025-10-23; last author)
- Homework/CTF-style environments as evidence of real capability. 
  > "Especially when using benchmarks to evaluate dangerous capabilities, evaluations using homework-style exercises can yield significant differences from evaluations using real-world data."  
  > -- `research__autoadvexbench_benchmarking_autonomous_exploitatio_27715bcb` (2025-03-03; first author)
- "Our attack didn't find it, so it's safe." 
  > "the failure of current attacks should not be seen as proof that aligned text models remain aligned under adversarial inputs."  
  > -- `research__are_aligned_neural_networks_adversarially_aligned_c19aad5c` (2023-06-26; first author)
- Stale evaluations on older models. 
  > "a conclusion that "LLMs cannot reliably find kernel bugs" drawn from a test against models released six or more months ago is actively misleading for current threat modeling."  
  > -- `research__llms_now_find_zero_days_autonomously_what_it_means_a82d6d05` (2026-04-13; solo author)
- Field conventions adopted without justification. 
  > "These are directions where someone (usually someone famous!) published an influential paper that got something critical wrong with the approach, methodology, or evaluation... and then the rest of the field followed along the same wrong direction without thinking critically about the initial choice"  
  > -- `research__how_to_win_a_best_paper_award_or_an_opinionated_ta_54221651` (2026-03-09; solo author)
